# L-0001 Attack the premise before the next fix (2026-11-20)

applies-to: both (self-loop skill item 2; ExampleApp supervisor)

What happened: the authorized_keys migration took judge rounds 27–31 (seven actor rounds), each closing blockers and
revealing finer ones (concurrent writer, last name of an inode, rotation, stale receipts, record trust, removal races).
Every fix assumed one premise: ExampleApp must automatically rewrite earlier ExampleApp member key lines.
Premise test (one git query): member key lines existed only on the unmerged test branch for about an hour
(43b93bc → c03d610); no shipped build ever wrote them. The premise was false; the work served no real installation.
Change it led to: lead ruling T (upgrade obligations follow what shipped; ExampleApp never writes the SSH key file); actor
round 35 deletes the machinery; critic batch 25 migrates the cases.
Raised by: the lead (the loop) before the owner, prompted by the owner's earlier reframes and pstack's
"attack the premise". The blind backtest's trajectory reviewer (run-3, snapshot 15) independently proposed
"DELETE: cut upgrade promises to what was actually delivered".
Mechanise: trajectory alarm "same area ≥ 3 rounds" → reviewer must write the shared premise and the observation that
would differ if it were false, before another fix is briefed.
